summary: This component displays a Bluesky engagement widget for an article, showing how many people are already talking about it and offering options to share or engage. It tries to find an existing Bluesky post matching the article (either from frontmatter or by searching the account's history), and only renders the widget once that lookup is complete to avoid showing a button that might disappear.

explanations.9: This function builds the text that appears above the engagement buttons, changing the message based on whether we found a post, are still looking, or already have engagement data.
explanations.20: If there's no record key (no Bluesky post found), we show a generic invitation to share the article.
explanations.23: We treat both 'still loading' and 'failed to load' the same way — we don't want to claim nobody has reacted when we simply don't know yet.
explanations.31: We're storing the count in a variable so we can use it twice in the next line without calling .length again.
explanations.32: We pluralize the message correctly: 'person is' for 1 person, but 'people are' for any other count.
explanations.43: This hook tries to find the Bluesky post ID either from frontmatter or by searching the account's post history; resolving is true while that search is happening.
explanations.44: We're creating a new metadata object that merges the original data with the found record key, so child components see the complete picture.
explanations.53: While we're still searching for a matching post, we return null to render nothing — this prevents a jarring flash of a share button that disappears once we find the post.
explanations.73: We only show the engagement UI (likes, replies, etc.) if the data successfully loaded; if the post was deleted or unreachable, we skip this section.
